body:
ecbench solver reports were limited to u128, and some BigUint adapters dropped recoveries above a narrower width. This change carries recovered values through 256 bits with ExactScalar, preserves the legacy number-through-u64/decimal-string encoding, and uses exact parsing plus subgroup reduction before checked narrowing in runner and audit verification. BigUint overflow now returns an explicit error. [pcc:unverified]

Validation: the actual-crate ecbench suite reported 517 passed, zero failed and five ignored; the full-library gate reported 6063 passed, zero failed and 130 ignored in 1493.16 seconds. Both ecbench and ic_autolab entrypoints passed cargo check. New tests cover full-width report serialization, overflow rejection, nullable records and high-bit-preserving verification. Retained logs, failed attempts and source hashes are in research/curve25519_autolab_parity_20261105/transport-integration/. All execution results are unsigned producer observations. [pcc:unverified]

Separate, unregistered candidates prepare bounded rejection sampling and actual Curve25519 workload construction. Native harnesses and fresh replays reported 32 and five passing tests respectively. The workload harness reuses actual Fp256/Curve25519 source with an extracted group ledger/trait and an unused panic-only Fp64 shim; its scope is documented alongside all attempts. [pcc:unverified]

Full-width workload orders and solver dispatch are the next integration branch. This PR contains no comparative experiment or speedup claim. Official PCC claim/ledger registration remains pending the existing exclusive reservation, last reported as T-1649; no signed standing is asserted. [pcc:unverified]
title: Carry full-width recovered scalars through ecbench reports and verification
